text: What did the gipsies do on the night Julia died?
why: Watson asks in ¶91 what the gipsies did, and the context is Julia's death.

text: What did the gipsies do on the night Julia died? — they made the whistles, as signals
id: q.what_gipsies_did=they made the whistles, as signals
why: Holmes links the night whistles with the gipsies in ¶90, and Helen attributed the whistle to them in ¶41, so this is a reasonable possibility.

text: What did the gipsies do on the night Julia died? — they got at her through the window, raising a shutter bar
id: q.what_gipsies_did=they got at her through the window, raising a shutter bar
why: Holmes suggests in ¶90 that the clang may have been a shutter bar falling back into place, which invites the idea of entry by the window.

text: What did the gipsies do on the night Julia died? — nothing: they had no part in it
id: q.what_gipsies_did=nothing: they had no part in it
why: This is a plain alternative; Helen only guesses at their involvement, Holmes was unsatisfied in ¶65, and nothing establishes a role for them.

text: What did the gipsies do on the night Julia died? — there are nearly always some of them in the plantation, so their being there that night shows little
